scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

injection.command:
ip link set eth0 down
  ip link set eth1 down

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP
ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.
scoring_axes: must-identify-affected-links: BOTH spine uplinks down -- eth0 (to spine_router_0_0) AND eth1 (to spine_router_0_1)

bonus-notes-host-link-fine: explicitly rules out the host access link / pc_0_1 itself (eth2 UP, gateway pingable)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Both fabric uplink interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 — eth0 (172.16.0.7/31,
connected to spine_router_0_0:eth2) and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, connected
to spine_router_0_1:eth2) — were brought administratively DOWN at
2026/08/04 11:45:10. The kernel shows both interfaces in state DOWN with
no UP or LOWER_UP flags and only the BROADCAST/MULTICAST flags set,
confirming they were shut down at the OS level (e.g. via
`ip link set eth0 down; ip link set eth1 down`).

With no L2 path to either spine, leaf_router_0_1's BGP daemon cannot
establish TCP sessions to 172.16.0.6 or 172.16.0.10; both sessions are
stuck in the Active state and FRR internally logs "No path to specified
Neighbor" as the reset reason. The host-facing interface eth2 (10.0.1.1/24)
remains UP, which is why pc_0_1 can still ping its local gateway but
cannot reach anything beyond the leaf. Because both spine peerings are
lost, leaf_router_0_1 installs no BGP-learned routes and advertises
10.0.1.0/24 to nobody — causing a complete fabric black-hole for all
traffic to or from pc_0_1.

The spines show the sessions as Established only because BGP Graceful
Restart helper mode is preserving stale forwarding state within the
configured 360-second stale-path timer; they will withdraw those routes
once the timer expires.

Root cause: eth0 and eth1 on leaf_router_0_1 were forced administratively
down, severing both uplinks to the spine layer simultaneously.

Corrective fix: Restore the interfaces with `ip link set eth0 up` and
`ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. BGP will re-open both eBGP
sessions within one connect-retry interval (~18 s), exchange prefixes,
and full fabric reachability will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names leaf_router_0_1 as the affected device and attributes the interface shutdowns and BGP loss to that router.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names both fabric uplinks as down: eth0 to spine_router_0_0 and eth1 to spine_router_0_1, matching the required affected links.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes eth2 remains UP and explains pc_0_1 can reach its gateway but cannot reach beyond the leaf, matching the required symptom distinction.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-host-link-fine: explicitly rules out the host access link / pc_0_1 itself (eth2 UP, gateway pingable)
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states eth2 is UP and pc_0_1 can ping its gateway, ruling out the host access link as the cause.
Recommends bringing eth0 and eth1 up on leaf_router_0_1 using 'ip link set ... up', which matches the expected fix and will restore the uplinks and BGP sessions.

The investigator's logs clearly show both eth0 and eth1 on leaf_router_0_1 are DOWN, leaf BGP neighbors are Active while the spines report Established, and eth2 is UP — supporting the conclusion that loss of both uplinks caused the outage. A minor unsupported inference is the claim that the interfaces were explicitly administratively shut and that Graceful Restart helper with a 360s timer explains the spine behavior (those specifics aren't shown in the log).
